title: Dynamic weight smoothing and automated rollback for multi-region hosted API rollouts
creator: Ava Martin
description:
Background: Recent regional rollouts uncovered abrupt traffic oscillations and transient SLO violations when shifting weights during blue/green swaps. Current controller increments weights in fixed steps and immediately drains traffic which amplifies momentary load spikes and KV-cache churn across replicas.

Problem: We lack a robust smoothing layer and automated rollback triggers that are sensitive to cross-region latency, token-per-request cost spikes, and cache-miss amplification during weight changes. This increases customer-facing tail latency and complicates on-call responses during rollouts.

Goal: Implement a dynamic weight-smoothing controller and automated rollback automation that: 1) applies sigmoid-based weight interpolation to avoid step spikes; 2) observes regional KPIs (p99 latency, error rate, per-token CPU/GPU utilization, prefix cache-miss); 3) enforces soft/hard SLO gates with backfill isolation; 4) provides deterministic escalation paths (canary -> ramp -> full) with automated safe rollback when correlated KPIs breach thresholds.

Design proposal:
- Weight smoothing: replace fixed-step increments with time-windowed interpolation using configurable curves (linear, sigmoid, log). Default to sigmoid with 3-parameter tuning (steepness, midpoint, duration).
- Telemetry windowing: compute short (30s), medium (5m), and long (15m) aggregates for p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, cpu/gpu utilization, and prefix KV cache-miss rate.
- Multi-metric gating: define gating rules that combine metrics with weights (e.g., 0.5*p99 + 0.3*5xx_rate + 0.2*cache_miss_delta). Thresholds configured per-release channel (canary, staged, lts).
- Adaptive rollback: when gate breaches for X consecutive windows, perform automated roll-forward to previous stable weight or full rollback to last healthy deployment. Rollback includes an enforced cool-down window and optional auto-ticket creation with attached telemetry snapshot.
- Regional backfill isolation: during rollbacks, prevent cross-region traffic bleed by pinning tenant routing for affected regions to regional LTS instances and allowing background backfill at reduced concurrency.
- Safety overrides: operator can trigger manual override which pauses smoothing and uses immediate drain (admin only).

Acceptance criteria:
- New smoothing controller deployed to staging and exercised with chaos tests that simulate sudden capacity loss; smoothing prevents >25% p99 spike compared to baseline.
- Automated rollback triggers in 80% of simulated SLO breach scenarios in staging.
- Observability: dashboard showing weight curve, gates, and telemetry snapshots for each rollout. Runbook updated and linked.
- Unit/integration tests covering curve parametrization, gate evaluation logic, and rollback FSM.

Runbook & links: will add runbook to Console > Runbooks > Rollouts. Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14286. Design doc: https://docs.internal.redwood/rollouts/dynamic-smoothing (internal).

Risks & mitigations:
- Overly aggressive rollback sensitivity -> false positives: mitigate with hysteresis and longer medium window.
- Increased control-plane complexity -> ensure feature flag gating and incremental opt-in per region.
- Cache thrash during backfill -> throttled backfill and KV-prefetch heuristics.

Notes: This ticket focuses on controller logic and telemetry gating. Separate follow-ups will cover UI controls in Console and Dedicated capacity policy alignment.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Triage: Reviewed with Release Eng and Platform SREs. Identified cache-miss amplification as primary risk. Agreed to prototype smoothing curves before full rollout.
2026-02-22 - Design review: Presented sigmoid/default parametrization. PM asked for per-tenant opt-out flag; adding as config with low exposure.
2026-03-03 - Implementation update: Core weight interpolator implemented (prototype). Added unit tests for curve edge cases. PR opened: merge request referenced in description.

2026-03-08 - Staging test: Ran chaos test simulating regional pod kill. Observed 18% p99 improvement vs fixed-step but noticed increased 95th percentile for certain request sizes; investigating KV-cache prewarm path.
2026-03-10 - Blocker discovered: Need a small change in routing layer to support transient pinning during rollbacks. Split into follow-up: ENG-78690 (routing pinning).
